+Response Bodies
+---------------
+
+Pass a string or bytes to :class:`.Response` for a complete body. A string is
+encoded as UTF-8. A :class:`collections.abc.Sequence` of bytes, such as a list
+or tuple, is also a buffered body. Werkzeug can calculate its byte length and
+set the ``Content-Length`` header automatically. Any other iterable is streamed,
+even if it defines ``__len__``. This avoids consuming a stream to calculate its
+length when sending headers.
+
+Iterable chunks must be bytes. Passing strings or other nonbytes chunks is
+deprecated and will be removed in Werkzeug 4.0. Encode text chunks as UTF-8
+before yielding them::
+
+    def generate():
+        yield "Hello, 世界!".encode("utf-8")
+
+    response = Response(generate())
+
+Reading :attr:`.Response.data` can buffer a streaming body into a list. This
+can be disabled with :attr:`.Response.implicit_sequence_conversion`. When an
+iterable is converted to a list, including by :meth:`.Response.freeze`, its
+``close`` method is called immediately after consumption. Callbacks registered
+with :meth:`.Response.call_on_close` still run when the response is closed.
+
+:attr:`.Response.stream` is deprecated and will be removed in Werkzeug 4.0.
+Use :class:`io.BytesIO` to build a body incrementally, then pass its
+``getvalue()`` to ``Response``. The
+:attr:`.Response.automatically_set_content_length` setting is also deprecated
+and will be removed in Werkzeug 4.0; length will always be calculated when
+possible. Use a streaming iterable when automatic length calculation is not
+wanted.

"""Check each Werkzeug deprecation at its public operation."""
import os
import warnings


def observe(operation):
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        result = operation()
    return result, [str(w.message).lower() for w in caught if issubclass(w.category, DeprecationWarning)]


def run(case, response_type):
    if case == "preserve":
        def ordinary():
            r = response_type([b"a",b"bc"])
            original = r.get_data(),r.calculate_content_length()
            r.set_data(b"abc")
            return original,r.content_length
        value, observed = observe(ordinary)
        valid = value == ((b"abc",3),3) and not observed
    elif case == "mixed":
        chunks = [b"a", "é", b"c"]
        operations = (lambda: response_type(chunks).get_data(),
                      lambda: b"".join(response_type(chunks).iter_encoded()))
        results = [observe(operation) for operation in operations]
        value = [data for data, _ in results]
        observed = [messages for _, messages in results]
        valid = all(data == "aéc".encode() and any("mixed" in w or ("bytes" in w and "str" in w)
                    for w in messages) for data, messages in results)
    elif case == "stream":
        r = response_type()
        stream, observed = observe(lambda:r.stream)
        # Independently verify continuation. A warning from write or get_data
        # cannot supply evidence for the property access above.
        stream.write(b"ab")
        value = r.get_data()
        valid = value == b"ab" and any("stream" in w for w in observed)
    elif case == "length":
        r = response_type()
        def explicit_length():
            r.automatically_set_content_length = False
            r.set_data(b"abc")
        _, observed = observe(explicit_length)
        value = r.content_length
        valid = value is None and any("automatically_set_content_length" in w or
                                     ("automatic" in w and "length" in w) for w in observed)
    else:
        raise ValueError("unknown public operation " + case)
    print(case,repr(value),observed)
    return valid


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from werkzeug.wrappers import Response
    raise SystemExit(0 if run(os.environ["PANEL_STAGE"],Response) else 42)
